judges.verdict: This is a premium, cohesive real-time scene. The environment layout, colour grade, framing, UI overlay and cursor-orbit behaviour are close to the reference: region colours sit within about 10 levels, the orbit frames have no doubled mountains, and nothing is wrong at the bottom at rest. The p05 vortex is a real wow moment. The gap to 10 sits in the hero object and a few surfaces. (1) The rings look like milky acrylic or gel, not carved, frosted ice, and this is glaring once the camera dollies in during the hold. (2) The orb is a blown-out white bulb, with no glass shell and no plasma inside. (3) At the sustain pose the opened halves of ring A are seen end-on and read as two plastic lumps with flat cut caps. (4) The mountains look like smooth clay, not rocky alpine peaks, and the dark mountains show low-poly facets when the cursor orbits the camera. (5) The mid- and near-ground water has an under-filtered corduroy ripple pattern that will shimmer in motion and leaves a ragged band at the bottom of the hold frame. A demanding art director would flag all five at a glance side by side. Every one can be fixed with shader work or Blender re-bakes; none needs a render blend.
strengths: Environment layout and composition match ref_F000 almost one-to-one: main peak within about 7 px, iceberg, floes, foreground rocks and ripple centre all in place. Keep the camera, FOV and plate layout exactly as they are.
Colour grade and exposure are near-reference (region_stats: sky top +2/+2/-2, peak snow +2/+5/+1, corners BR 0/+1/-1). Do not re-grade globally.
Rest and eye ring poses match the loop frames closely (cmp_q00_rest, cmp_q03_eye): the band, the outer rings and the dark ring-joint bands are in the same places as the reference.
Bottom of frame at rest (y 506-766) matches the reference closely: rocks, snow caps and right-hand floes are all present, with no seams or odd shapes.

Cursor-orbit frames are clean. In ptr_left the parallax is coherent (far peak shifts about 135 px, the nearer iceberg about 115 px). In ptr_bottom_right the left and right horizons have no doubled mountains, the mist layers stay consistent, the floe reflections are correct and the bottom is clean.
The UI overlay is essentially identical to the Figma frame: logo, nav, headline size and leading, subline, 'Scroll to Explore' and Sound position (crop_ui_rest_copy).
p05_expand gives a striking spiral 'portal' around the orb: graphic, readable and award-worthy as a composition. The camera dolly and hold fog read well.
The iceberg waterline is clean with a soft mist band (ptr_bottom_right right horizon), and floe reflections in the planar mirror are believable.
The shards' cobalt hue and scale match the reference, and the clouds and sky are soft and believable.

issues.title: Ice ring material reads as milky acrylic or gel, not carved frosted ice
issues.evidence: crop_q00_rest_hero.jpg: the engine band (left, x~90-475, y~205-295) is a rounded, tube-like slab covered in big soft blue-white blotches (camouflage-like, low-frequency). The reference band (right, x~650-1035) is a flat slab with crisp darker bevel lines at both ends (x~705 and x~990), fine frost grain and milky internal scatter. Zoom of q03_eye.png (560-880 x 170-570) against loop_F045: the engine rings look like clear blown glass with white lumpy smears; the reference shows chiseled, frosted ice with darker blue absorption in thick sections and fine crackle. sweep/sw_hold_BL.png (470-1070 x 140-640) at dolly-in: the rings are opaque-ish milky acrylic or soap. There is almost no background refraction through the bands, no internal fractures, no clear-versus-frosted zones, flat lighting and foam-like cut ends. The reference close-up (crop_p06_sustain_hero.jpg, right) shows carved ice with sharp light-catching edges and cracks. In p05_expand.png the top arc (475-855 x 40-190) is a smooth, nearly opaque tube.
issues.suggested_fix: Rebuild the ice surface in layers. (a) Bake the artist's Cycles ice-shader detail into per-ring normal, frost/roughness mask and thickness maps (2K) in Blender. (b) Add a tri-planar high-frequency micro-frost normal masked so about 40% of the surface is frosted (roughness 0.35-0.5) and about 60% is clear (roughness 0.05-0.1). (c) Add Beer-Lambert absorption by thickness: cyan-blue in thick sections, near-white at thin rims. (d) Add an inner fracture/crack layer (parallax or refraction-offset baked crack texture). (e) Use split, harder normals at face-to-bevel transitions so the band reads as a chamfered slab, not a smooth tube. (f) Desaturate the baby-blue tint about 15% toward neutral grey-cyan. Replace the current low-frequency blotch normal entirely.

issues.title: Orb is a blown-out white bulb, with no glass shell and no plasma inside
issues.evidence: q03_eye.png orb core 60x60 at (695,340): engine luma mean 243, sd 10.5; loop_F045 mean 223, sd 25.3, so the engine is brighter with less than half the internal structure. Mean RGB of 60x40 at (690,350): engine 238/245/248, reference 200/216/231. The 2x zoom shows a crisp glass-shell rim, cyan-mint tint, white cloud/plasma forms inside and a faint iridescent fringe in the reference; the engine shows a featureless pearl. In p05_expand.png and p06_sustain.png (620-820 x 290-490) the orb is a clipped white disc with a halo that reads as a sun or light bulb.
issues.suggested_fix: Render the orb as a glass shell (Fresnel rim, slight refraction, faint thin-film iridescence) around an inner animated plasma volume: 2-3 layers of curl-noise or fbm density, raymarched or as stacked billboards, white with cyan/mint edges. Tone-map the core to about 0.9 so the inner structure survives, and raise the bloom threshold or cap its intensity during the hold so the disc never clips to flat white.

issues.title: Sustain hold loses its shape: opened halves seen end-on read as plastic lumps
issues.evidence: p06_sustain.png: the two halves of ring A sit at (355-485, 315-485) and (945-1090, 320-490). They are seen nearly end-on and read as shapeless white 'marshmallows' beside rings B, C and D, which sit close to their rest pose, so the 'opened' state does not read. Their flat, smooth elliptical end caps look like cut foam or plastic. p04_expand_pop.png shows the same: a flat cylinder-end cap at about (557-615, 445-540) beside the diagonal band. The reference crop_p06_sustain_hero.jpg (right) shows large, clear C-arcs with crisp fractured ends. p05 reads very well (vortex), so the problem depends on the phase.
issues.suggested_fix: Keep continuous slow rotation but bias the opened halves so their arc planes stay within about 30 degrees of the view plane during sustain (roll about the view axis or add a face-on counter-rotation). Push the opening offset so the arcs clear the core silhouette, as at p05. Replace the flat cut caps with fractured, faceted break ends (jagged geometry or a break normal map, plus bevel and bright edge transmission).

issues.title: Mountains look like smooth clay snow, not rocky alpine peaks; low-poly facets show on orbit
issues.evidence: 3x zoom of q00_rest.png against ref_F000 (260x200 at 150,190): the engine peak is a smooth, creamy, clay-like snow mass with rounded ridges. The reference shows dark striated rock gullies, crisp ridgelines and alpine texture. Region 120x80 at (230,240): low-frequency tonal sd after a 6 px blur is 14.9 in the engine against 21.4 in the reference, about 30% less tonal structure. In ptr/ptr_bottom_right.png (0-320 x 200-420) the dark left mountains show flat triangulated facets with smooth gradients, a low-poly read, once the cursor orbits the camera.
issues.suggested_fix: Re-bake the mountain textures in Blender with a slope- and curvature-driven rock/snow material: exposed dark rock on faces steeper than about 45 degrees, snow on ridges and gentle slopes, AO in the gullies. Bake a high-res normal from a subdivided, displaced high-poly onto the runtime mesh. Alternatively, camera-project ref_F000's mountain detail into the bake and blend it with the current bake for faces the reference camera cannot see. Smooth or add normals on the dark mountains to hide the facets.

issues.title: Water normals under-filtered: corduroy streaks mid-ground, ragged band at the bottom during the hold
issues.evidence: q00_rest.png 200x90 at (880,470): high-frequency energy (mean |x - blur1.5|) is 3.01 in the engine against 0.93 in ref_F000, 3.2x. In other regions the ratio is only about 1.2x, which codec softening explains. At 4x this shows as a regular, high-contrast horizontal corduroy ripple pattern with pixel sparkle, where the reference is calm, milky glass with fine low-contrast grain. p06_sustain.png 240x70 at (880,690), at 6x: the outer ripple band breaks into stair-stepped 1-2 px horizontal streaks. At 1x the bottom strip (y 720-766) reads as a soft milky smear with a ragged right edge, where ref_F420 shows crisp, dark-blue small wavelets. The bottom of the frame is the client's sensitive zone, and this will shimmer in motion.
issues.suggested_fix: Enable anisotropic filtering (EXT_texture_filter_anisotropic, 8-16x) on the ripple and normal maps. Fade normal amplitude and raise roughness with distance or normal variance (Toksvig-style). Use a finer, more isotropic noise in the far field, and clamp glint sparkle before the resolve. In the near field (bottom about 80 px) add crisp, small dark-blue wavelets like F420 in place of the soft swell.

issues.title: Weak aerial perspective: distant ice too crisp, thin mist at the iceberg base
issues.evidence: q00_rest.png iceberg 300x90 at (960,330): low-frequency contrast sd 42.8 in the engine against 36.1 in ref_F000 (+19%), and the region_stats iceberg is +10/+12/+8 brighter. The distant ice cliffs (x 1110-1440, y 300-400) are bright, crisp white in the engine but hazy and soft in the reference. The iceberg-base mist band is about 15 px tall in the engine (y ~435-450) against about 40 px of soft haze in the reference (y ~420-460).
issues.suggested_fix: Raise distance fog on far geometry by about 10-15%, lifting shadows toward the sky colour with depth. Add a gentle depth-based softening for anything farther than the iceberg, approximating the reference's lens and air. Make the waterline mist card at the iceberg base about 2x taller with a softer top falloff.

issues.title: Specular and refraction aliasing on ring silhouettes
issues.evidence: 4x nearest-neighbour zoom of q03_eye.png (575-735 x 175-375): the outer ring shows 1-px white specular slivers, broken streaks and a stair-stepped silhouette; loop_F045 is smooth and soft there. p04_expand_pop.png inner ring silhouette (about 565-600 x 310-400) is speckled. Include the sculpture in the temporal AA (reproject with ring motion vectors), or supersample the sculpture pass 1.5x on T1.

issues.title: UI details: Sound glyph and headline during the hold
issues.evidence: crop_ui_rest_sound.jpg: the engine shows a flat line before 'Sound'; Figma shows a sine-wave glyph. issues.title: Shards look slightly opaque and low-poly
issues.evidence: crop_q00_rest_hero.jpg (left): engine shards are opaque cobalt with flat facets and hard white facet highlights. Reference shards (right, e.g. x~990-1060, y~120-180) are translucent with a soft inner glow and lighter, refracted facets.

judges.verdict: From a distance the ice is in the right place. Its overall brightness, pale cyan-blue hue, ring proportions and segment joints match the reference, and the orb and environment are refracted through the rings. Up close, though, it reads as polished glass, gel or acrylic, not carved frosted ice. The surfaces are smooth and carry broad 30-80 px blurred cloud blotches and long brush-like streaks. There is almost no frost, inclusion or crack detail. Silhouettes are smooth tori where the reference is lumpy and chiselled, and facet glints are missing. The gap is worst in the hold and expand poses, which are the client's signature interaction with the camera dollied in. There the ring pieces look like soap or marshmallow blobs with flat, untextured end caps and liquid-chrome contour reflections. Thin ring edges and inner rims also alias (stair-steps, dotted 1-px speckles, dotted streaks), which will crawl in motion. The front band is too milky to show ring D behind it in q02, the deepest dark refracted bands are missing, and the thin rings are about 20-33% more saturated than the reference, which runs greyer than its sky. All of this is fixable with shader work plus geometry and texture bakes in Blender. None of it needs a render blend.
strengths: Global value range of the ice matches the reference closely; do not brighten or darken it globally. q00 front band (250x55 at 600,350) luma mean 192.1 vs 193.2, 10th/90th percentile 172/217 vs 173/215. q03 whole sculpture (300x385 at 578,178) mean 182.3 vs 183.0.
Hue family is right: pale cyan-blue ice, median hue 305-307 vs 303-309 in the reference, with the same overall pale, airy look.

Ring proportions and thickness at rest are correct. The front band reads as a chunky slab with a hairline Fresnel highlight on its top edge and a darker inner-wall strip at its left end (crop_q00_rest_hero.jpg x~135-147).

Segment joints (the dark cross-bands where ring segments meet) are present and land where the reference has them: in q03 at the top-right and bottom-right of the outer ring (crop_q03_eye_hero.jpg engine x~220-260 y~60-70 and y~330-345 vs reference x~720-760).

Background and orb refraction inside the rings works. In q01 the inner horizontal rings show the refracted bright orb and white icebergs/mountains much like the reference (crop_q01_loop15_hero.jpg engine x~200-350 y~200-245 vs reference x~780-910).
No 8-bit banding: contrast-stretched smooth gradients on p06 (band and segment cap) show clean dithered ramps. No black or NaN pixels in any ice region (lowest luma 67-149).
At contact-sheet scale (sweep.jpg, about 40 frames covering intro, hold, pop, release and the idle tumble) the rings read consistently as ice, with no flicker, black holes or broken materials.

issues.title: Ice surface reads as smooth glass/gel with smeared cloud blotches; missing frost, inclusions and cracks
issues.evidence: crop_q00_rest_hero.jpg, front band: the engine (x150-420, y215-280) shows broad soft 30-80 px blotches (blurred refraction of sky and clouds) and long smooth streaks. The reference (x710-980, same y) is an evenly frosted face with 3-15 px mottling, fine horizontal streaks and cloudy inclusions. zoom_ice_material/q00_band_2x.png. crop_q02_loop30_hero.jpg, band: the engine (x200-460, y195-295) has only horizontal smears; a luma stretch (zoom_ice_material/q02_band_behind_stretch.png) shows no micro-texture at all. The reference (x760-1020) has dense frost mottling and a dark internal crack at x830-853, y227-253. p06_sustain.png, band x520-940 y400-510: smeared cloud blotches, like brushed acrylic. ref_F420.png, central ring x450-930 y300-450: frost inclusions, chipped edges and crisp refracted orb streaks at x600-820 y410-440. p05_expand.png, top arc x515-815 y45-130: wavy white contour lines that read as liquid chrome or molten glass, not ice. Average luma matches (q00 band 192 vs 193), so the gap is texture and character, not exposure.
issues.suggested_fix: Add mid- and high-frequency ice structure, and stop the large-scale refraction from forming readable cloud shapes. (1) Bake per-ring maps in Blender from the reconstruction: a frost/inclusion density map (cloudy white patches plus fine streaks along the ring, with features about 3-20 px at 1440 width) and a thin crack-line mask. Alternatively compute them in object space in the shader (3D Voronoi edge distance for cracks, fBm for frost) so they rotate with the ring. (2) In IceMaterial, use frost density to raise the transmission blur (sample a lower mip or a larger kernel of the transmission target), to add a whitish forward-scatter mix toward about #dfe9f3 at 15-35% in frosty patches, and to drive a mid-frequency normal perturbation. (3) Cut the amplitude of the low-frequency normal and refraction offset that makes the 30-80 px blotches by about 50-60%, and blur the refracted sky more so clouds never read as shapes inside the band. (4) Draw the cracks and inclusions with 2-3 parallax layers so they sit inside the ice, with a thin dark core and slight bright edges.

issues.title: Hold/expand pieces look like soft soap or marshmallow blobs with flat, untextured end caps
issues.evidence: p06_sustain.png, left outer-ring piece x355-485 y315-490: smooth waxy shading with rounded, melted-looking ends. Its end cap (x430-462, y380-485) is a flat plane with a smooth luma gradient of 165-197 and no frost, normal or refraction detail even under a 6x luma stretch (zoom_ice_material/p06_eng_leftseg_stretch.png). The right piece (x1000-1090, y320-490) is the same. Polygon facets show on the left piece's top silhouette. p05_expand.png: the top arc's end cap (x805-855, y95-145) is a clean, flat light-blue face, and its left tip (x475-545, y145-190) is a rounded nub. Reference ref_F420.png: the top block (x380-765, y50-235) and right segment (x855-1140, y150-560) are thick chiselled ice with flat-cut fracture faces, frost, crisp bevels with white glints (x735-765, y90-130) and visible internal depth (zoom_ice_material/p06_leftseg_pair.png, p05_pair_2x.png). The dolly-in at the hold puts these caps large on screen, so they are the most obvious CG tell in the hero.
issues.suggested_fix: Rebuild the segment break faces in Blender as irregular fracture planes (Cell Fracture, or a boolean with a Voronoi-displaced plane), with a small 1-2 mm bevel and proper UVs, then bake the same frost, crack and normal maps onto them. In the engine, check that the cap faces actually receive the full ice shading (transmission, frost, normal map). Their constant gradient suggests collapsed UVs or a separate material group without the maps. Add inner-wall absorption darkening on the caps and a crisp bright bevel highlight along cap edges. Remove the rounded, melted tips.

issues.title: Ring silhouettes and surfaces too smooth and regular; reference is lumpy and chiselled
issues.evidence: q00_rest.png vs ref_F000.png, ring A bottom arc x570-870 y470-535 (zoom_ice_material/q00_bottomarcs_3x.png): the engine outline is a smooth, regular torus. The reference outline is scalloped, with lumps every 25-35 px and flat chiselled facets. crop_q01_loop15_hero.jpg, ring A left side: the engine (x120-200, y60-400) is a smooth tube with a soft gradient. The reference (x680-760) has a notched, faceted outline with planar facets (zoom_ice_material/q01_ringleft_2x.png). The inner ring B's top outline in q00 (zoom_ice_material/q00_topleft_4x.png) is smooth in the engine and bumpy in the reference. Ring D's edge-on end in q02 is rounded in the engine and squared-off and chipped in the reference.
issues.suggested_fix: Apply a cellular (Voronoi F1 / flat-cell) displacement to the ring meshes in Blender and re-export them. If polycount must stay low, bake a high-to-low normal map. Target amplitude is about 3-6% of the tube radius, producing flat facets with crisp ridges and an irregular outline with lumps every 25-35 px at the rest framing. Keep normals nearly flat within each facet so speculars break up along crests. Use the artist's original EXPORT.blend displacement or sculpt detail if it exists.

issues.title: Aliased ring edges, hairline rims and high-frequency streaks (will crawl in motion)
issues.evidence: q03_eye.png, outer ring top-left silhouette x565-640 y185-310: stair-stepped edge with isolated bright and dark single pixels along it, plus white dotted contour lines inside the ring at x600-680 y200-270 (zoom_ice_material/q03_topleft_4x.png, q03_crest_pair_4x.png). q01_loop15.png, ring A inner edge x612-622 y290-400: a 1-px jagged bright-plus-dark double rim (zoom_ice_material/q01_innerrim_pair_6x.png). p06_sustain.png, ring A lower-left arc x510-690 y500-640: aliased dotted white streaks running along the ring (zoom_ice_material/p06_eng_ringA_lowerleft_3x.png). q00_rest.png, ring A lower edge x650-800 y515-528: a dotted, zipper-like edge. Reference edges are continuous and clean. Sharper-than-H.264 detail is fine, but the speckle and stair-step pattern will shimmer as the rings tumble.
issues.suggested_fix: Render the ice into the MSAA target, or cover it with the existing temporal AA using neighbourhood clamping. Widen and filter the Fresnel rim (a broader smoothstep on N dot V, faded with fwidth). Band-limit the micro-normal streaks by screen-space derivative (a Toksvig/LEAN-style roughness increase and reduced normal amplitude where fwidth(uv) is large, with mip-mapped normal maps). Clamp or fade the refraction offset near silhouettes so the transmission lookup never samples across the depth discontinuity, which is what makes the 1-px bright and dark speckles.

issues.title: Front band too milky: ring D behind it is not visible through the ice
issues.evidence: crop_q02_loop30_hero.jpg: ring D passes behind the front band. The reference (x810-980, y195-290) clearly shows ring D's diagonal edges and a dark crack through the band. The engine (x250-420, y195-290) shows nothing of ring D, only horizontal smears (luma stretch in zoom_ice_material/q02_band_behind_stretch.png). The engine band is also brighter and milkier: region 300x60 at (590,335), luma mean 187.6 vs 180.3, saturation 18.0 vs 21.3 against loop_F030.png. In q01 (crop_q01_loop15_hero.jpg, engine x110-260 y150-350), ring A likewise shows almost no structure of the rings behind it, while the reference shows mottled structure through ring A.
issues.suggested_fix: Check that the behind-rings transmission pass actually includes ring D when it sits behind the band in this pose. It appears to drop out completely. Lower the band's scatter and milky veil in its clear regions, keeping frost only in patches from the frost map, so refracted rings read through it with a modest offset. Let the band's luma drop about 5-7 levels in q02 as a result.

issues.title: Deepest dark refracted bands are missing, and ring C reads as a thin ribbon
issues.evidence: q03_eye.png, outer ring right side (50x200 at 818,260): engine luma min/10th percentile 123/130 vs loop_F045.png 70/119. The reference's long dark steel-blue refracted band along the ring is weak in the engine. crop_q00_rest_hero.jpg, band end walls: the reference has crisp dark vertical lines at x~705 and x~997 (y205-290). The engine has only a soft dark strip at x~135-147 and nothing at the right end (x~410). crop_q03_eye_hero.jpg, ring C across the orb: the reference (x~660-835, y~180-245) shows a darker top face and inner wall, so it reads as a thick slab. The engine (x~160-350, y~180-245) reads as a thin pale ribbon.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a total-internal-reflection and absorption-path term. Where the exit ray (refract() on the back face) would totally internally reflect or graze, sample the darker lower hemisphere (water and mountain base) or blend toward a steel blue around #6f86a6. Raise the absorption coefficient so long internal paths (ring walls seen lengthwise, band ends) reach luma about 70-100. Make the band-end inner walls crisp dark lines, and give ring C a visibly darker top face or inner wall.

issues.title: Thin rings too saturated and slightly violet; missing the cyan-green orb tint
issues.evidence: Matched regions, measured with ffmpeg signalstats (limited range): q00 ring A top (160x22 at 640,218) saturation 20.1 vs 15.9 and ring A bottom (160x22 at 640,500) 19.7 vs 14.8. q01 ring A left (50x250 at 570,220) 13.2 vs 9.9 and right (40x200 at 830,240) 17.5 vs 14.4. q03 left ring (40x200 at 590,260) 21.2 vs 17.5. Meanwhile the engine sky is less saturated (12.7 vs 14.2), so the sculpture-to-sky saturation ratio is 1.35 in the engine vs 1.01 in the reference (q00). Median hue is 306-307 vs 303-306, slightly more violet. The reference has a cyan-green orb-light tint on the bottom inner surface of ring B (ref_F000.png x~705-760 y~472-488) and through ring C (loop_F045.png x~640-820 y~365-395). The engine is plain blue there, with saturated painterly blue streaks on ring A and B (zoom_ice_material/q00_bottomarcs_3x.png).
issues.suggested_fix: Lower the absorption-tint saturation by about 20% on the thin rings (A and B) and shift the hue 3-4 degrees toward cyan-grey, keeping luma unchanged. Add a subtle cyan-green tint around #c4f1e8 where orb light passes through the inner rings (weight it by an orb-facing or orb-proximity term). Soften the saturated blue streaks on rings A and B.

issues.title: No specular facet glints; only uniform hairline rims
issues.evidence: loop_F045.png x610-680 y225-265: a chain of bright facet glints along the chiselled crest of the outer ring. ref_F420.png x735-765 y90-130: a bright bevel glint on a cut face (zoom_ice_material/ref_glints.png). In the same crest region of q03_eye.png (x580-700, y200-290) the engine shows only thin, aliased hairline streaks and no glints. The p06 and p05 caps and edges have none either.

Keep them filtered so they don't alias.

judges.verdict: The global grade is essentially locked. Full-frame mean sRGB is within 1-2 levels of the reference and saturation is identical in every compared pose. The midtone curve matches (rest luma p25/p50/p75 165/194/210 vs 164/193/209), there is no banding even under a 5x contrast stretch, the vignette matches, and the idle orb exposure and bloom match almost pixel for pixel. What still separates the engine from the reference is post and atmosphere, not white balance. (1) The dolly-in hold has no depth of field and its fog bank does not build. The reference pulls focus to the sculpture (mountains and iceberg go soft) and grows a thick, billowing mist up the left mountain while the iceberg stays deep slate-blue. The engine keeps the background tack-sharp, shows only a thin flat band, and greys the iceberg out by 20-26 levels. (2) In the hold the orb clips to a flat neutral-white 'sun' disc (sd 9.6, B-R 4.8) where F402 shows a bright plasma with internal filaments and a cyan limb (sd 25, B-R 15). (3) At rest the mid-ground floes are the crispest, darkest-edged thing in frame (3.2x the reference's high-frequency energy, blacks 30 levels deeper). The left-foot mist is a flat opaque band while the iceberg's waterline mist is too thin, and the near ripple field is milkier and less blue. Rest and eye alone would score about 8.7; the hold is about 7.3; weighted, 8.2. All of it is fixable with a DOF pass, Atmos card work, orb emission and tone-curve tuning, and small bake or shader grades. judges.verdict: The layout, sky, clouds, iceberg silhouette, right-hand range and foreground rocks match F000 closely, and the real baked geometry holds up under the hold dolly and the cursor orbit: no stretching, tearing or doubled mountains. Side by side, though, the environment still looks CG. The mountains look like smooth clay, the dark left ridge is faceted and the wrong shape, and there is no lens defocus where the reference has one. The middle of the lake has a fine 'corduroy' ripple where the reference is a calm, glossy mirror with long vertical reflection smears. The mist at the iceberg's waterline is too thin at rest. In the hold, a fog veil washes out the iceberg (+27 levels), while the fog at the mountain base stays flat instead of F420's dense, billowing bank.
strengths: Composition and placement match F000 almost exactly: main peak at about (290,207) in both, iceberg crest at about (1195,328) in both, and the right-hand silhouettes (tall berg, iceberg, far range) within 2-5 px in every 10-px column from x=885 to x=1435. The foreground rocks, snow boulders and right-hand ice chunks are in place.

Region colours mostly sit within about ±10 levels: sky top 198,208,221 vs 196,206,223; peak snow 194,211,231 vs 192,206,230; corners TL/BR, mid-left and mid-right match; bottom-left boulder 67,95,132 vs 67,98,137; right snow mound 180,188,202 vs 178,184,200; upper iceberg face 64-73 vs 73-79.
The sky gradient and cumulus cards look right: same shapes, softness and brightness (cloud core 218,223,231 vs 213,220,234), with no halos or card edges.

Real geometry with baked textures survives the p06 dolly-in and the pointer orbit (ptr_left, ptr_bottom_right): no plate stretching, no floe or rock tearing, no doubled mountains, believable parallax. The bottom of the frame at rest is clean.

Planar reflections of floes and icebergs are present and correctly placed (vertical streaks under the slabs), and the concentric ripple ring is centred under the sculpture with the correct ellipse proportions and number of rings.

Snow on the foreground rocks and the granular texture of the right snow mound match the reference well, and the main peak's mean tones along a vertical column stay within about 10 levels of the reference.

issues.title: Mountains look like smooth clay; the dark left ridge is faceted and the wrong shape; the foothill is white instead of dark rock
issues.evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-muhamadrifaldi-Documents-GitHub-retrux-hero-rnd/a0f5735b-9a7f-477e-9b57-6de40ca5644b/scratchpad/p3/r11_3/zoom_environment/peak_q00_vs_F000.png and .../zoom_environment/ridge_shape_q00_vs_F000.png. In q00_rest.png the main mountain (150-560, 200-450) has soft, rounded ridges and evenly lit snow. ref_F000 has crisp ribs and couloirs with dark navy rock exposed in the gullies. Dark left ridge (0-190, 275-440): the engine shows flat, low-poly facets with thin crease lines, body colour 45,63,96 vs reference 35,56,90, and after a sigma-2.5 blur its contrast is SD 29.0 vs 43.6. The engine has a pointed peak at (22,279) and a long shoulder at y 306-310 for x 95-135, which is 25-60 px too high and hides part of the white secondary peak (reference at x 100-145, y 295-315). Add subdivision and displacement so no facets show. Re-bake the mountains in Cycles with a material driven by slope and curvature: dark blue-grey rock (about sRGB 35,55,90) on faces steeper than about 40° and in couloirs, snow on ledges and crests, and a slight highlight on ridge lines. Bake at 4K for the main peak and the ridge. Turn the foothill at (350-530, 400-450) into dark rock with a snow cap. Let the mist at the base show rock streaks through it rather than a uniform wash.

issues.title: Hold fog is wrong: a veil bleaches the iceberg while the fog at the mountain base stays flat (p06 vs F420)
issues.evidence: p06_sustain.png vs ref_F420.png, with .../zoom_environment/p06_iceberg_vs_F420.png and p06_leftmtn_vs_F420.png. Iceberg face (1170-1270, 500-570) is 105,129,158 in the engine vs 78,108,144 in F420. Along column x1180-1240, y 500-575, the engine reads 93-117 R vs 74-86 in the reference. At rest the engine iceberg face (64-73) matches the reference (73-79), and the reference iceberg does not change between F000 and F420, so the hold fog (fogHold=1) adds about +30-40 levels that the reference does not have. The far right range is also +10 too bright. Meanwhile, F420's fog at the left mountain base is a dense, billowing bank, and wisps climb to mid-height over the mountain's lower half. Blurred SD in (0-330, 480-580) is 30.2 in the reference vs 21.8 in the engine. issues.suggested_fix: Change fogHold from a distance veil into a local height fog: put its ceiling at about 1/3-1/2 of the left mountain's height and modulate its density with slowly scrolling fbm noise (2-3 octaves), or use 3-5 soft billow sprites that hug the left mountain base and the space between the ranges. Leave the iceberg and the right range out of it, or cap the hold's added haze there, so the iceberg face stays near (78,108,144). Add one faint wisp on the main mountain's mid-flank. Ramp it with the dolly so it builds rather than pops.

issues.title: No lens depth of field: background and near rocks are pin-sharp, which exposes the CG
issues.evidence: .../zoom_environment/sharpness_ring_vs_far.png. In ref_F000 the ring at (530-650, 330-410) is crisp, while the far floe slab at (930-1050, 440-520) has 3-4 px soft edges. Because the blur depends on depth within one frame, it is DOF, not H.264 softness. The engine is 1-px sharp on both. The reference mountains, iceberg, clouds and even the near rocks (fgrocks_q00_vs_F000.png) are defocused, and F420 has stronger background blur still, while p06 is pin-sharp. This sharpness exposes the dark floe contact lines, the corduroy wavelets and the faceted ridge.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a cheap depth-based defocus. Render the environment, then apply a half-res separable gaussian or bokeh blur with circle of confusion from linear depth: focus at the sculpture's distance, about 2.5-3 px maximum at 1440 px for the far field (mountains, iceberg, floes), and about 1-1.5 px for the near-foreground rocks. Increase it slightly as the hold dolly moves in, to match F420. Composite the sculpture and shards sharp on top, or exclude them via depth or stencil, and blur the water's reflection target consistently.

issues.title: Middle and far lake read as rippled 'corduroy' instead of a calm glossy mirror with long vertical reflections
issues.evidence: .../zoom_environment/leftshore_q00_vs_F000.png (water at 0-110, 490-550), reflection_q00_vs_F000.png (530-585), and p06_rightwater_vs_F420.png. The engine draws a uniform, high-frequency horizontal wavelet pattern across the middle and far lake, and it breaks floe reflections into short, broken streaks of about 20-30 px. In the reference the middle and far water is calm and milky-glossy, and the floe reflections are long, soft vertical smears (in F420 about 55-80 px under the slabs at 1080-1150, 655-710). Fine wavelets appear only in the reference's near water. At 4x, the engine hold water shows horizontal pixel-run streaks (p06_floerefl_4x.png).

Sample the planar reflection with a vertical anisotropic blur (5-9 taps along screen-Y, length growing with distance) so reflections stretch into long, soft streaks. Use mip-biased or filtered normals at grazing angles to stop the horizontal streaking. Lift the far water slightly toward the milky haze colour (far floes region is 162,182,208 vs 172,189,208).

issues.title: At rest, the iceberg's waterline mist is too thin and too low; the lower iceberg stays dark and its base edge is crisp
issues.evidence: .../zoom_environment/iceberg_q00_vs_F000.png and waterline_right_q00_vs_F000.png. Along column x1080-1120 in ref_F000, the lower iceberg from y 405 to 445 is washed by mist (101-124, 128-146, 161-172). In the engine it stays dark (64-69, 96-99, 135-137) down to y≈425, and its mist only ramps from y 430 to 460, leaving a crisp dark bottom edge at about y 435. Raise its opacity at the waterline to about 0.5-0.55 of a haze colour around (170,185,205), fade it smoothly upward, and break it up horizontally with soft noise, so the bottom 40% of the iceberg seems to emerge from fog as it does in F000. issues.title: Ripple ring under the sculpture is soft and low-contrast; the orb glint is neutral and sits too low
issues.evidence: .../zoom_environment/ripple_q00_vs_F000.png and glint_q00_vs_F000.png. The engine's rings are soft grey shadow bands: the outer trough at (560-860, 575-589) is 175,189,211 vs 145,162,192 in the reference, and blurred SD in (440-1000, 560-700) is 14.4 vs 20.2. The reference rings have bright, crisp crests, cobalt troughs and a choppy inner zone. The reference glint is cyan (176-182, 194-199, 216-220) and sits on the ripple crests at y 669-706. The engine glint is neutral (179-187, 191-198, 206-213), made of separate sparkle dots, and about 25 px lower (y 693-736). Near water is about 11 levels darker (167,181,201 vs 177,189,209). In the hold, filter the ring's normal at grazing angles so the outer ring reads as a wave crest rather than a smeared band.

issues.title: Mist plume at the summit is missing

judges.verdict: Intro, idle tumble and release are close to glitch-free: no tears, holes, doubled mountains, hard fog bands, ring-through-ring intersections or sky/fog banding. The hold and pop (dolly-in) states carry two artefacts a demanding art director would flag. First, the bottom ~50 px of every dolly-in frame is a smeared light band whose dark patches have stair-stepped texel edges and pixel speckle. This is exactly the "weird bottom of frame" the client warned about; F420 shows crisp wind-wave crests there. Second, every opened arc ends in a flat, uniformly shaded, low-poly cap that reads as cut plastic pipe, where F420 shows bevelled, refracting ice faces. Smaller items: a bullseye-like sustain pose, a flat grey rock wedge in the pop corner, UV-seam dark ticks on floes, grey smudges on the hold orb, and the headline still visible in the hold sweep frames (to verify).
strengths: Fog over the mountain bases in the hold is soft, as in F420. p06_sustain (0-560, 480-600) is a smooth gradient with no hard band; 1-px column scans at x=60 (y 340-640) and x=1300 (y 0-340) contain no flat run of 6 px or more, so there is no banding in fog or sky. The iceberg-base mist is soft in hold_L/TR and intro_3.
No doubled silhouettes when the cursor orbits the camera: the left mountain and the iceberg are single and parallax-consistent across sw_hold_L, sw_hold_R, sw_hold_TR and sw_hold_BL.

Waterline / far-shore edge is cleanly anti-aliased even dollied in (p06_sustain 480-840 x 600-612); ring silhouettes have 1-2 px AA transitions with no stair-stepping against the sky (sw_hold_TR 960-1080 x 200-320).
No ring-through-ring interpenetration in any hold, pop or release frame inspected, and shards never pierce rings (sw_hold_B 850-970 x 170-300).
The opened shape reads beautifully as an exploded vortex in sw_hold_T, sw_hold_TR and sw_pop_B, close in spirit to F420's arcs.
Idle tumble tau_0.25..3.75 and the intro frames are clean: near rocks, floes and the concentric ripple ring at rest show no tearing or stretching, and the bottom strip at rest is crisp.

Arc joint seams on the rings at rest match the reference's segment joints (loop_F015/F045 show the same transverse joint lines), and the dark end contours of edge-on bands match loop_F000. These are not glitches; keep them.
The peak wisp on the left mountain matches ref_F000.

issues.title: Smeared, stair-stepped near water / foreground band at the bottom of every dolly-in frame
issues.evidence: p06_sustain.png: across the whole bottom strip y=716-766 there is a light band with a hard-ish top edge near y=716-723 and dark-blue smeared patches. At 4x nearest (zoom p06_bot_br4x, x 1000-1360, y 676-766) the patch borders are horizontal stair-steps of 2-8 px runs x 1 px rows, plus speckle. Same in the centre (zoom p06_bot_bc4x, x 300-660, y 723-766). sw_hold_L: (1200-1440, 715-745) and (0-600, 706-766) show the same stepped streaks. sw_pop_B: (960-1440, 673-740) and (480-960, 660-720) show blocky stepped patches and salt-and-pepper speckle (zoom popB_steps4x, x 1060-1300). The stack of all six hold bottoms (zoom hold_bottoms.png) shows it in every hold frame. Reference ref_F420 has the same light foreground band at y=716-766, but as crisp, smoothly curved dark-blue wind-wave crests on light water (zoom bottom_p06_vs_ref.png). The animated ripple will make the steps crawl.
issues.suggested_fix: Find which layer draws this band (planar-mirror RT vs. baked near shelf vs. lake-bed through low Fresnel) and fix its resolution and filtering. (1) Render the mirror RT at 1.0x drawing-buffer resolution on T1, or at least 0.75x with LinearFilter plus a 1-2 px separable blur. Never sample it with nearest. Clamp or fade the ripple UV offset within ~40 px of the screen edge. (2) Add a near-field wind-wave normal (2 scrolling octaves, amplitude rising toward the camera) so the foreground breaks into F420's dark wave crests instead of a smeared cloud reflection. (3) If it is a baked shelf or lake-bed texture, re-bake it in Blender at 2-4x texel density for the hold camera distance and enable anisotropy 8-16 plus mipmaps.

issues.title: Opened arc ends are flat, uniformly shaded, low-poly caps (cut-plastic-pipe look); side chunks read as puffy blobs
issues.evidence: Each cap is a single flat light-blue plane with no refraction, frost or edge highlight, and its silhouette is 8-10 straight polygon segments: sw_hold_R left-chunk cap (400-437, 293-393) and right-chunk cap (970-1003, 283-393) (zoom holdR_bandends3x); p06_sustain left-chunk face (420-487, 330-487) and right cap (1004-1040, 375-490) (zooms p06_ringL, p06_xR4x); sw_hold_L bottom-arc end (837-910, 648-683) (zoom holdL_botarc); sw_hold_TR top-arc end (895-955, 100-168) (zoom holdTR_toparc4x); sw_hold_BL (487-545, 280-355), an octagonal flat face plus a thin fin (zoom holdBL_l4); sw_hold_B (665-720, 485-557) is a flat white disc and (815-890, 120-200) another cap; sw_pop_B (540-570, 470-540). The side chunks in p06 (355-490, 315-490; 945-1090, 318-490) look like smooth marshmallow blobs. ref_F420's cut ends (360-440, 235-350; 930-1020, 335-440) are bevelled, faceted ice with internal refraction and bright edge glints.
issues.suggested_fix: Give the cap faces the same ice shading as the tube: normal perturbation and frost, refraction or thickness term, and Fresnel rim. If the caps lack UVs, use triplanar projection. Add a small chamfer or bevel to the cap rim so it catches a specular line. Raise the tube cross-section segment count to 24 or more (or smooth the cap outline) so no polygon corners show at hold distance. Add internal crack or bubble detail to the caps. This can be done by re-exporting the arcs from the Blender reconstruction with a Bevel modifier and proper cap UVs, then applying the existing IceMaterial normal/thickness path to the cap material group.

issues.title: Sustain pose reads as a flat bullseye with stubby 'ear-muff' side chunks instead of an opened gyroscope
issues.evidence: p06_sustain: two concentric face-on vertical rings (485-950, 150-640 and 540-910, 250-550) frame the orb dead-centre, with a horizontal band across (490-990, 395-530). The opened outer ring shows only as two end-on stubs (355-490, 315-490; 945-1090, 318-490), so the 'open' shape barely reads. sw_hold_R has the same arrangement (495-950, 140-640). In ref_F420 the central ring is at roughly a 3/4 tilt with arcs encircling it, and sw_hold_T / sw_hold_TR / sw_pop_B already read as a clear vortex.
issues.suggested_fix: Bias the hold so the inner rings are never within about 20 degrees of face-on at the end of the dolly. Either add a fixed 25-35 degree tilt offset to the expand frame, or phase the slow-motion idle rotation so the sustain lands at 30-50 degrees. Open the outer arcs within the view plane (tangentially or screen-radially) so they are not seen end-on as stubs.

issues.title: Flat, untextured grey-blue rock wedge at the bottom-left corner during the dolly (pop); flat slate faces on the near rock at release

judges.verdict: Both of the client's red lines hold under cursor orbit. In all 10 ptr poses no mountain is doubled or ghosted, there are no plate edges, holes, seams or 1-px border lines, and the edges revealed at az ±4.9 deg are fully modelled and textured. Parallax is depth-correct: going from ptr_rest to ptr_right, distant peaks shift about +150 px, the iceberg +114 px, and the floes less. What keeps the score below 9 are small glitches that show up on close inspection or in motion. (1) The far water has hard-edged pale blotches and 1-px stair-stepped ripple dashes. (2) Near-black single pixels jump along the 1-px front edge of the flat ice sheet left of the sculpture (2-4 per pose, down to RGB 2,3,8), and also sit on stray sliver geometry. (3) When the pointer is near the bottom edge, a flat, near-black navy notch slides into the bottom-right corner. That is exactly the 'something weird at the bottom' the client warned about. (4) Smaller items: a comb of dark ticks on a far floe, faint sawtooth marks in the mist at the iceberg base, and dotted aliasing on the ring refraction lines. Shaders, bake padding or a re-bake, and retouching can fix all of these; none needs a render blend.
strengths: No doubled or ghosted mountains in any of the 10 poses: levels-stretched skyline bands (y 150-480) and edge-detect maps show single, consistent silhouettes, and the parallax is depth-correct (real 3D, no projected plates). Keep this exactly as it is.

Frame edges are clean in every pose: the 60-px left/right strips and the top and bottom rows show no holes, plate ends or stretched texels, and the border row/column averages match their neighbours (no 1-px lines). The newly revealed far-left ridge (ptr_right, ptr_top_right, ptr_bottom_right) and far-right horizon/snow mound (ptr_left, ptr_top_left, ptr_bottom_left) are fully modelled.

The sky has no banding (dither grain only) and no cloud-card edges, even under a strong levels stretch. The horizon mist band is a smooth gradient with no card edges or intersections with mountains in any pose.

Silhouettes are well anti-aliased: at 4x the main left peak and the iceberg cliff have soft 1-2 px edges with no stair-stepping. There is no z-fighting and no NaN blocks, and a firefly scan found no bright outliers apart from one ridge texel.
The lake stays coherent in every pose: concentric ripples, glint and the sculpture reflection move correctly, nothing is doubled, and there is no sky gap at the horizon line.
The orb push-in (camera z 11.79 to 9.56) keeps mountains, floes and rocks crisp, with no texel stretching or magnification blur.
The bottom 120-px strip at rest and in every ±az/±el pose shows no bake seams, tone breaks or stretched texels on the foreground shelves and rocks (apart from the down-tilt notch in issue 3).

issues.title: Far-water mottling: hard-edged pale blotches and 1-px stair-stepped ripple dashes that will crawl when the cursor orbits
issues.evidence: ptr_rest.png box x420-560,y462-482 (strongest at x487-553,y463-476): pale irregular 'map-outline' patches on otherwise smooth water. Along y=470, luminance jumps between adjacent pixels on flat water (182->188, 191->181, 178->188, 181->193), which is hard 1-px edges, not soft reflection. Below them are horizontal 1-px stair-stepped ripple dashes. ptr_left.png x280-420,y465-485 and ptr_right.png x522-580,y462-487 show the same blotches with a different shape and position, so they change with the camera and will shimmer during the orbit. ref_F000 in the same box is smooth, soft water with soft vertical floe streaks. Zooms: zoom_glitch_cursor_orbit/FARWATER_eng_ref3x.png (engine top, reference bottom), W_refl4x_rest/left/right.png, W_shape4x_right.png.
issues.suggested_fix: Band-limit the water normal perturbation in the far field. Scale the ripple and micro-normal amplitude by distance, or by fwidth(uv), so it fades out before the band at screen y≈455-500. Sample the planar-reflection render target from a blurred mip with a roughness ramp over distance instead of one sharp tap. Extend the waterline temporal AA to the whole lake band (about y 450-600) so what remains does not crawl.

issues.title: Near-black single-pixel specks jumping along sub-pixel edges (ice-sheet rim, floe comb, rock slivers)
issues.evidence: Speck scan (pixel darker than all 8 neighbours by >35 luma): 2-4 per pose, mostly on the 1-px navy front edge of the flat ice sheet left of the sculpture. ptr_right (703,537) RGB 6,14,27; ptr_bottom_left (577,510) RGB 3,6,14, (601,511) RGB 2,3,8 and (562,510); ptr_rest (616,536) and (485,542); ptr_left (560,537); ptr_top (610,562); ptr_top_left (597,564); ptr_top_right (664,561); ptr_bottom (491,515); ptr_bottom_right (662,508) and (699,510); ptr_orb (618,574). The edge line itself is about 80-107 luma; the specks are 3-68. The same specks appear on the far-right floe comb (ptr_bottom (1279,455), ptr_top_right (1377,510)) and on needle slivers of the foreground rock right of centre (ptr_right (934,750), ptr_bottom (1011,716)). Their position changes from pose to pose, so they will twinkle as 'crawling ants' along the edge while the cursor moves. Zooms: zoom_glitch_cursor_orbit/BLACKPX8x.png, SPECKS8x_grid.png.
issues.suggested_fix: Most likely cause: sub-pixel side faces fetching the empty (black) atlas background at coarse mips. Edge-pad every baked .webp atlas (Blender bake margin 16-32 px with Extend, or a push-pull fill of the empty background) and regenerate the mipmaps from the padded image. Guard the shader against degenerate normals or NaN (no normalize(0); clamp the minimum albedo). Weld or delete sliver triangles on the ice-sheet rim and the rock crest. Let the temporal AA cover the lake band.

issues.title: Flat near-black navy notch slides into the bottom-right corner when the pointer goes to the bottom edge
issues.evidence: ptr_bottom.png x1237-1440,y743-766: a rounded dark crescent wall cut by the frame edge. ptr_bottom_left.png x1327-1440,y730-766, with a pale floor (#93a4b9) visible inside like a hole. ptr_bottom_right.png x1130-1218,y752-766, plus a sliver at x1310-1440,y759-766. The wall colour is #13365d-#1a3f6a (luma about 55): flat, untextured, and the darkest, most saturated patch in the frame, darker than any shelf notch visible at rest (#2c4969-#3f5370). It sits just below the frame in ptr_rest, so it only appears on the downward pitch (el -1.18 deg). It is plausible geometry (a melt pool or notch in the foreground shelf), but it reads as a dark blob or hole at the bottom edge, which is the client's explicit red line. Zoom: zoom_glitch_cursor_orbit/BRSTACK_bottoms.png (rest / bottom / bottom_left / bottom_right).
issues.suggested_fix: Re-bake that foreground notch with lighter walls (more indirect bounces and an AO lift so it reads as lit ice like the other notches), or fill or reshape it in the reconstruction, since the reference camera never showed it. Alternatively, cap the downward pointer pitch at about -0.6 deg, or add a faint bottom-edge haze so the notch never enters the frame.
